LabDesignSystem.title: The Construction on Tracing Paper
LabDesignSystem.thesis: A geometric proof in progress — compass arcs, dimension lines, and construction marks on cream draughting paper. Every element is placed with the deliberateness of a technical drawing: no decoration that isn't also structural, no colour that isn't also information.
LabDesignSystem.colors_intro: One accent used by rule. All other colour is tonal variation of graphite on cream. No colour enters the system without a named rationale for what information it carries.
LabDesignSystem.type_intro: Three typefaces, each chosen for a specific information register. STIX Two Text carries the intellectual authority of mathematical typesetting. Spectral carries sustained readable argument. Departure Mono carries the precision of measurement without personality.
LabDesignSystem.type_specimen_body: AI in Education · Human-Computer Interaction · Frontend engineering
LabDesignSystem.atoms_preview_intro: Shared UI atoms. Each is documented with live specimens and state annotations.
LabDesignSystem.tag_filter_drawer_desc: Collapsible frequency-sorted tag browser with chip display, drawer search, and tier grouping.
LabDesignSystem.molecules_preview_intro: Molecules compose atoms into stateful interaction patterns. The filter drawer, for instance, encapsulates tag selection, frequency grouping, and open/close state behind a single clean interface.

LabAtoms.page_intro: The smallest reusable units of the design system. Each atom encodes a single visual contract — class composition, state behaviour, and accessibility semantics — so higher-level components compose without adding style decisions.
LabAtoms.nav_link_intro: One atom for all inline navigation. Combines the label class with a persistent ghost underline — always visible, not revealed on hover. Active and current positions use a non-link span with aria-current=page, never a styled anchor.
LabAtoms.section_label_intro: The label hierarchy atom. Renders as any heading level or span, always in the label class (Space Mono uppercase). The active prop applies the active-mark class — used once per surface for the current section identity.
LabAtoms.named_rule_card_intro: Documents a named design invariant. Name in label class, statement in medium body weight, optional rationale in caption. Flat by construction — border structure only, no shadows.
LabAtoms.state_rest: Ghost underline (0.5px), ink-secondary text. Always identifiable as a link — not only on hover.
LabAtoms.state_hover: Underline darkens to ink at medium weight (1px). Text shifts to ink. Animated via transition-colors.
LabAtoms.state_focus: Global red outline — 1px solid compass-arc red, 3px offset. Consistent across all interactive elements.
LabAtoms.state_current: Non-link span with aria-current=page and active-mark class. One red per surface — the One Red Rule.
LabAtoms.filter_input_intro: A controlled search and filter input. The border is always present at ghost weight — it never appears or disappears, only shifts colour on focus. Used by the ADR register search and the tag drawer inner search.
LabAtoms.state_filter_rest: 1px ghost-colour border — always visible, never zero
LabAtoms.state_filter_focus: Border shifts to active red on focus — the One Red Rule for interactive widgets
LabAtoms.state_filter_filled: Border returns to ghost; value renders in ink-secondary

NamedRuleCard.one_red_statement: The compass-arc red appears exactly once per surface — on the single element that is active, current, or selected.
NamedRuleCard.one_red_rationale: A second red on the same surface means the first was wrong. Its rarity is the point: it marks the foreground construction element, nothing else.
NamedRuleCard.no_decoration_statement: If removing an element makes the surface less informative, it was earning its place. If it makes it calmer, it was decoration.
NamedRuleCard.no_decoration_rationale: Every mark on the drawing earns its place or is removed. This is not minimalism — it is maximum information, zero noise.
NamedRuleCard.flat_by_construction_statement: No shadows. Depth from line weight and tonal ramp only — heavy lines are closer, ghost lines are background.
NamedRuleCard.flat_by_construction_rationale: A shadow here would be a smudge on the drawing. Depth is achieved through graphite weight hierarchy: heavy (1.5px), medium (1px), ghost (0.5px).

LabMolecules.page_intro: Molecules are multi-atom components with encapsulated interaction state. Each molecule is documented with a live interactive specimen, key design decisions, and its full prop API.
LabMolecules.tag_filter_drawer_intro: A collapsible frequency-sorted tag browser. Tags are grouped by count tier and rendered at five type sizes — larger type signals higher frequency, count badges reinforce the signal. The drawer opens in page flow between the filter bar and the table, keeping layout stable.
LabMolecules.frame_empty_desc: No tags selected, drawer closed. The “No tags selected” hint occupies the chip zone. The TAGS toggle is always present, ready to open the drawer.
LabMolecules.frame_active_desc: Two tags selected, drawer closed. Active chips with × remove buttons appear in the tag zone. The TAGS badge shows the count. CLEAR becomes visible at far right.
LabMolecules.decision_layout_note: Search anchored left · TAGS trigger + chips fill centre · CLEAR at far right. CLEAR reads as global reset, not search clear.
LabMolecules.decision_chips_hide_label: Chips hide when drawer is open
LabMolecules.decision_chips_hide_note: Active chips collapse when the drawer opens — the drawer shows selected state directly via filled chip style. One affordance per action.
LabMolecules.decision_none_note: Tag-scoped clear deselects all tags without touching the search input. Positioned far-right in the drawer header — same spatial grammar as CLEAR in the toolbar, narrower scope.
LabMolecules.decision_frequency_note: Five type-size tiers (w1–w5) and count badges are dual signals — size encodes frequency at a glance, badge gives the precise number.

LabColors.page_intro: One accent used by rule. All other colour is tonal variation of graphite on cream. No colour enters the system without a named rationale for what information it carries.
LabColors.color_ground_usage: The ground. Every surface begins here. Warm, not clinical — the colour of cream draughting paper, not office-white. The word calques (French: tracing paper) is the name of the PhD software; this ground makes that etymology visible.
LabColors.color_ink_usage: Primary lines, headings, body text. The weight of a freshly-sharpened pencil. Not pure black — graphite on cream reads as precision, not harshness.
LabColors.color_ink_secondary_usage: Secondary annotations, labels, dates. The weight of a second-pass construction line — used for Departure Mono labels, supporting metadata, and dimension annotations.
LabColors.color_ink_ghost_usage: Tertiary grid lines, dividers, construction guides. The weight of a preliminary mark — present enough to structure the page, quiet enough not to compete with content.
LabColors.color_active_usage: The single active construction element per surface — current position, selected era, focused project. Never used for decoration. Its rarity is the point: when the eye finds it, it has found the foreground element.
LabColors.color_active_named_rule_body: The compass-arc red appears exactly once per surface. A second red means the first was wrong. Applied on this surface to the active breadcrumb segment — “Design System” — and nowhere else.

LabTypography.page_intro: Three typefaces, each chosen for a specific information register. STIX Two Text carries the intellectual authority of mathematical typesetting. Spectral carries sustained readable argument. Departure Mono carries the precision of measurement without personality.
LabTypography.specimen_title: 25 years of precise practice — two eras, one continuous proof.
LabTypography.specimen_body: AI in Education · Human-Computer Interaction · Peer-reviewed scholarship across seven institutions. Frontend engineering · Product UX · IoT & SaaS platforms at HubSpot, HiveMQ, Matillion. The portfolio spans two professional cultures — the rigour of peer review and the velocity of product shipping — and the visual language must hold both without favouring either.
LabTypography.rationale_display: STIX Two Text — the mathematical typesetting standard, designed for scientific journals and peer-reviewed papers. The italic cut carries a genuine geometric incline: not emphasis, but character.
LabTypography.rationale_headline: STIX Two Text italic at headline scale — used for section and project titles. The same incline as display, reduced to working size.
LabTypography.rationale_title: Spectral at medium weight — designed for screens, academic without stiffness. Holds position names and case study chapter titles without competing with the display face.
LabTypography.rationale_body: Spectral Regular — holds 65–72ch lines at 17px without fatigue. Pairs cleanly with STIX Two's scholarly register. The workhorse of the system.
LabTypography.rationale_label: Space Mono — distinctive tabular-figures monospace with instrument-panel character. Used for dimension annotations, dates, tick marks, and tech tags. A strong Google Fonts alternative to Departure Mono.
LabTypography.incline_rule_body: The display face carries a geometric incline — not italics as emphasis, but incline as character. Italic variants of the body face are reserved for titles of works (papers, products) only.
LabTypography.incline_comparison_body_label: Body italic — titles of works only
